newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian foreign minister leaves on Asian tour.
newsitem.headline: Russian foreign minister leaves on Asian tour.

text.p: Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov left Moscow on Monday on a nine-day Asian tour which will culminate in visits to Japan and China, a foreign ministry spokesman said.

Primakov was due first to go to the Central Asian state of Turkmenistan to attend a meeting of five foreign ministers from the region on the future of the Caspian Sea before visiting Mongolia from November 13 to 14.

He will meet Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda and Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto during a trip to Japan from November 15 to 17 and discuss when and where a Russo-Japanese government commission on trade and economic cooperation will next meet.
Itar-Tass news agency quoted diplomatic sources as saying Moscow had prepared proposals for "joint activities" on the disputed southern Kurile Islands but gave no details.
The four islands were seized by the Soviet Union at the end of World War Two and Japan wants Moscow to give them back. The dispute has kept Japan and Russia from signing a peace treaty.

In China from November 17 to 19, Primakov is expected to meet President Jiang Zemin, Premier Li Peng and Foreign Minister Qian Qichen to prepare a visit by Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin planned for the first half of next year.
Tass said talks may also cover preparations for an agreement on the reduction of the two countries' armed forces in the area around the long Russo-Chinese border.

The agency quoted well-informed sources as saying that, although differences remained on the issue, the agreement might be signed during a visit which Jiang is expected to make to Moscow in the second half of next year.
Relations between Russia and China have been gradually warming after a quarter-century freeze in ties following a wrangle over communist ideology. The freeze caused border clashes in the late 1960s.
Despite the improvement in ties, Russia and China do not expect to rebuild the alliance which linked them in the 1950s.
